article_title: Evidence for ESSA: OGAP Math Professional Learning System
citation: OGAP Math program description. (2024). Evidence for Learning. https://www.evidenceforlearning.org/ogap-math/
title: OGAP strand-based professional learning structure: cohorts of about 24 educators, four onsite days, and two follow-up coaching days
description: OGAP professional learning is organized by Strand, each aligned to a developmental progression in mathematics: Additive Reasoning (K–2), Multiplicative Reasoning (3–5), Fractional Reasoning (3–6), and Proportional Reasoning (6–8). Each strand is delivered to educator cohorts, often around 24 participants, through four onsite professional learning days, with districts able to space sessions several weeks apart. Two onsite follow-up coaching days, often during PLC time, "support transfer into classroom practice." Multiple strands may run simultaneously under the same structure.
requirements: Cohorts of about 24 educators per OGAP Strand
Four onsite professional learning days per strand
Two onsite follow-up coaching days, often scheduled during PLC time
constraints: Districts may choose consecutive sessions or a split schedule, with flexibility to space the sessions several weeks apart
target_learners: K–8 mathematics teachers participating in OGAP strands
target_learning_goals: Transfer of professional learning into classroom practice
Grade-band mathematical reasoning progressions (additive, multiplicative, fractional, proportional)
examples: Strands are aligned to grade-band progressions such as Multiplicative Reasoning (3–5) and Proportional Reasoning (6–8)
key_sources: OGAP Math program description. (2024). Evidence for Learning. https://www.evidenceforlearning.org/ogap-math/

citation: Bingham, W. V. (1916). Some Norms of Dartmouth Freshmen. The Journal of Educational Psychology, VII(3), 129-142. https://www.google.com/search?q=%22Some+Norms+of+Dartmouth+Freshmen%22+Bingham+1916
title: Ogive percentile norms charts for seven tests (Figures I-VII)
description: A set of seven percentile curves of distribution (Figures I-VII) charting the Dartmouth freshman norms for tapping, color naming, logical relations, mixed relations, cancellation, perception of form and endurance of grip. At each point the curve shows "the percentage of the group doing no better than the score there indicated", so a known score can be assigned a rank among one hundred classmates by reference to the chart. The endurance-of-grip data are additionally charted as an ordinary surface of frequency (Figure VIII) for comparison with the ogive form.
requirements: Requires scores from the same tests given under the described procedures, so an individual can be ranked against the 200-freshman group
constraints: No percentile charts are given for the memory tests because the scoring yields too few steps in the scale for relative-position comparison
target_learning_goals: mental abilities and performance measurement, including memory span, logical relations, sensory-motor speed and perceptual discrimination
examples: A student requiring 22.6 seconds on the color-naming test is read off the chart as rank thirty-third from the poorest among a hundred freshmen

article_title: Learning with our peers: peer-led versus instructor-led debriefing for simulated crises, a randomized controlled trial.
citation: Jaffrelot M, Boet S, Floch Y, Garg N, Dubois D, Laparra V, Touffet L, Bould MD. (2024). Learning with our peers: peer-led versus instructor-led debriefing for simulated crises, a randomized controlled trial. Korean J Anesthesiol. https://doi.org/10.4097/kja.23317
title: Ottawa Global Rating Scale (OGRS) for non-technical skills in simulated crisis management
description: The OGRS is a validated rating instrument for non-technical crisis resource management skills used as the trial's outcome measure. It "encompasses five main skill categories: leadership, problem solving, situational awareness, resource utilization, and communication," each scored 1-7 and summed to a total of 5-35, with behavioral descriptors anchoring each score. Two blinded raters achieved inter-rater reliability of 0.95 (P < 0.001).
requirements: Raters require training (six hours in this study, including scoring training videos and consensus discussion) and video recordings of the simulated scenarios.
constraints: The article notes prior OGRS data referred to post-graduate trainees, so undergraduate pilot data were unavailable at study planning.
target_learning_goals: assessment of non-technical crisis resource management performance
examples: Used to score pre-test, immediate post-test, and two-month retention videos in the randomized trial, blinded to randomization, test phase, and training level.
